subject: scorpion
pitch: A desert scorpion in a threatening pose, tail arched high over its back. Glossy amber armour with darker bands at every joint, big crab-like pincers held forward, eight thin legs, a segmented tail ending in a bulbous dark stinger, and a cluster of tiny black eyes on the head shield.
reasoning:
I need to work with the agentic-3js-builder SDK, sticking strictly to the documented APIs since I don't have full access to the rest of the library. I'm planning a scorpion design using the builder's joint, chain, sweep, part, stick, surface, ring, along, lathe, and extrude primitives, plus limb construction, while being cautious about painting features like spots, stripes, or countershading that may not be well-documented.

I'm also uncertain about b.ring and b.along signatures, so I'll avoid the riskier ones and rely on explicit joint/chain construction with sweep geometry for the legs instead, even though chain's exact path-to-joint behavior is unclear. For the scorpion's eight legs I'll build each as a three-joint chain with polyline paths swept into thin tubes, then move on to figuring out overall body coordinates and scale in meters.

Thinking through proportions, I'm settling on a stylized but realism-adjacent scale -- roughly 0.25m total length with a 0.2m tail height -- laid out along the Z-axis with the head forward and the tail arching back and up. I'm now defining the joint hierarchy: a root body joint, then a tailBase joint feeding into a chain that arcs backward and upward over the body before curving forward, mapping out the path points for that sweep.

Building the tail segments as tapering sweeps...

Adding ring bands at intervals...

I'm uncertain how the frame/aim orientation actually maps geometry axes, so I'll hedge by trying the frame-based approach for cylinders and torus bands, accepting some risk it may not align perfectly, and consider falling back to a stick-based method for the bands instead.

I'll favor constructing the body using scaled spheres via `part`'s `scale` option to build the ellipsoid shapes, rather than attempting an uncertain lathe-based outline approach.

Building segments with scaled spheres...

I'll assume chain(name, path) builds joints along a path and returns a Chain object, then sweep(chain, radius, {color}) gives it thickness. For the pincers, I'm planning a pedipalp chain extending forward and outward from the prosoma to form the claw arm, likely needing an extrusion for the pincer shape itself.

For the claw, I'm thinking palm as a scaled sphere with two tapered finger sweeps forming the pincer opening. For eyes, small black spheres placed explicitly at points clustered near the front-top of the prosoma, roughly three pairs positioned slightly off-center.

I'm deciding against surface-snapping functions since their API is uncertain, and instead placing eye spheres directly at explicit coordinates on the shield. Color palette settled: amber body, dark bands for contrast.

Now I'm working out body proportions, positioning the prosoma, mesosoma segments, and the start of the metasoma tail so legs reach the ground plane at y=0 while the carapace sits above it.

Mapping out the tail's arched curve with a chain of points rising up and curling forward over the body toward the head, setting up where the stinger will eventually hook down.

I'm adding a dark stinger bulb with a small spike at the tail tip, then building the tail as a curved sweep with radius tapering from thicker near the base to thinner near the stinger, debating whether to split into separate segments or use one chain for proper bending.

Adding the stinger geometry...

Skipping the spike, I'll go with a bulbous dark sphere and small tip instead. Now I'm laying out the four leg pairs with hip, knee, and foot points along the body, using thin amber chains with darker joint spheres at the knees for contrast, keeping feet near ground level.

Still writing pincer geometry...

I'm scaling up the pincer palms for a bulkier crab-like look, tapering the finger sweeps toward the tip, and adding dark banded tips to the claws. Now I'm placing the eye cluster on the front top of the prosoma shield, figuring out how to position it relative to the surface of that body part.

Adding dark seam rings at the joints between prosoma/mesosoma and mesosoma/metasoma using flattened sphere discs slightly larger than the body to simulate banding, plus extra band lines per mesosoma segment and similar joint markers for the pedipalps.

I'm skipping unused imports like rng since randomness isn't really needed here, relying on fixed material colors and roughness instead. I'm setting up the root body joint and leg chains, making sure feet rest near y=0, and adding the metadata export with the scorpion's name and description before defining a helper function for building ellipsoid body parts.

Now I'm picking out the color palette—amber tones for the carapace, dark brown for shadowed areas, near-black for the eyes, and a lighter amber highlight for a shield patch on top of the body—then moving into writing the pincer finger chains.

Writing joint chains...
